title: Only 11% Of Adults Can Pass This Train Driver Entrance Exam
summary: Explore railway observation and reasoning through clues, practical situations and fresh challenges.

landing.intro:
One railway challenge.
Could you pass it?

about.body: Connect the facts, notice the details and test your understanding of railway observation and reasoning. Each checkpoint reveals your topic profile before a different challenge begins.

steps: Read the clues and choose one answer.
See your topic profile at each checkpoint and continue to a new challenge.
Reveal your overall result, then optionally review the answers you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an official railway recruitment, medical, safety or employment assessment. Signals, rules and procedures vary by operator and jurisdiction.

stage-10.preAdCopy: Did you reach 80%? Your score and strengths are ready.

insights.overview: Your railway score at a glance

train-s1q1.question: What guides the wheels of a conventional railway vehicle?

train-s1q2.question: What is a railway point or switch used for?

answers.a1: Guiding a vehicle from one track route to another

answers.a2: An area beside the track used for boarding and leaving services

train-s1q4.question: Why do railway vehicles generally need substantial stopping distance?

answers.a3: Their speed, mass and wheel-rail adhesion limit how quickly they can stop
answers.a4: Stopping distance is always the same

train-s1q5.question: What is a coupling used for?

train-s1q6.question: What does traction refer to in railway operation?

answers.a1: The force used to propel the vehicle

train-s2q1.question: A display changes from 45 to 35. What change does it show?

train-s2q2.question: A log records a warning at 07:18 and an acknowledgement at 07:20. Which came first?

train-s2q3.question: A notice says “Platform 4 closed”. Which detail needs checking before directing passengers?

answers.a3: The number of windows in the station

train-s2q4.question: An indicator is unreadable. What is the sound response?

answers.a1: Cover it so it is no longer distracting
answers.a2: Assume it shows the usual value
answers.a3: Use the applicable procedure to resolve the missing information

train-s2q5.question: Two reports give different locations for the same obstruction. What needs clarification?

answers.a4: The exact location before relying on the reports

train-s2q6.question: A vehicle number is recorded as 4826 in one place and 4862 in another. What differs?

answers.a1: The first two digits are reversed
answers.a4: The last two digits are reversed

train-s2q7.question: A new vibration appears that was not present earlier. What should be recognised?

answers.a1: A reason to delete the earlier observation
answers.a2: A change that may need reporting and assessment
answers.a3: Proof of one specific fault without checking
answers.a4: A guarantee that the vehicle is safe

train-s3q1.question: Why must railway signals be interpreted using the relevant railway’s rules?

answers.a2: Signal meanings and operating systems can differ
answers.a3: Every colour has an identical meaning worldwide
answers.a4: A guess is sufficient on familiar routes

train-s3q2.question: An instruction to move is unclear. What should happen?

answers.a3: Clarify it through the authorised communication procedure

train-s3q3.question: Why are people kept away from restricted track areas?

answers.a1: Rails are safe whenever no vehicle is visible
answers.a2: Moving vehicles and railway equipment can create serious hazards

train-s3q4.question: What should a report of an obstruction on the line trigger?

answers.a1: An assumption that someone else removed it
answers.a2: A guess about whether it is small enough
answers.a3: The applicable safety and reporting procedure
answers.a4: A decision based only on the timetable

train-s3q5.question: Why must a departure check confirm that it is safe to move?

answers.a1: Closed doors guarantee every condition is safe
answers.a2: Boarding activity and other conditions may create a hazard
answers.a4: A familiar station cannot have a new hazard

train-s3q6.question: A safety-critical procedure has changed. Which version should be used?

answers.a4: Any old copy remembered by the driver

train-s3q7.question: Why should unusual equipment behaviour be reported accurately?

answers.a2: The information can support a safe assessment and response
answers.a3: A guess about the cause is always better than observations

answers.a2: The height of the station roof
answers.a4: The available grip between wheels and rails

train-s4q2.question: Why can wet or contaminated rails affect braking?

answers.a3: They make all stopping distances zero

train-s4q3.question: With other conditions equal, what does higher speed generally mean for stopping distance?

answers.a3: Exactly the same distance is needed

train-s4q4.question: A heavier moving vehicle at the same speed has more of which quantity?

train-s4q5.question: Why does a downhill gradient matter during braking?

answers.a1: The rails stop guiding the wheels
answers.a4: Gravity contributes a force along the direction of descent

train-s4q6.question: What is the purpose of a brake test required by the operating procedure?

answers.a2: To confirm specified aspects of brake function

train-s4q7.question: Why should braking be planned with a margin for conditions?

answers.a3: Actual adhesion and response may vary
answers.a4: The shortest possible stop is always guaranteed

answers.a1: The temperature at which water freezes
answers.a2: A force that opposes relative motion between contacting surfaces

train-s5q2.question: What does a lever turn around?

train-s5q3.question: Two meshed external gears turn together. If one turns clockwise, how does the other turn?

train-s5q4.question: What does a pulley change in a simple fixed-pulley system?

answers.a4: The direction of the applied force

train-s5q6.question: What does a spring generally do when compressed within its elastic range?

answers.a1: Stores energy and tends to return to its original shape

train-s5q7.question: Why can lubrication reduce wear between moving parts?

answers.a4: It makes all parts the same size

train-s6q1.question: An important instruction is unclear. What is the best response?

train-s6q2.question: What is the purpose of reading back a critical instruction?

answers.a1: To make the message longer for its own sake
answers.a2: To let the sender check that it was understood correctly
answers.a3: To replace carrying out the confirmed instruction
answers.a4: To transfer all responsibility to the sender

train-s6q3.question: Two tasks require the same person at the same time. What should be clarified?

answers.a2: Only the colour of the checklist
answers.a4: Which task has the shorter name

answers.a3: Only a reassurance that everything is fine
answers.a4: Relevant facts, unresolved concerns and the next required actions

train-s6q5.question: A colleague reports a new safety concern. What supports effective teamwork?

answers.a1: Hide it to protect the schedule
answers.a3: Dismiss it because the colleague is junior
answers.a4: Listen, clarify and address the concern

train-s6q6.question: A procedure changes. Which document should guide the task?

answers.a2: Any older copy that looks familiar
answers.a4: A remembered version from another organisation

train-s6q7.question: Why assign a clear owner to a follow-up action?

answers.a1: So responsibility and completion can be tracked
answers.a2: So nobody else may raise concerns
answers.a4: So the action becomes automatically complete

train-s7q1.question: A plan shows north at the top. A room is directly right of the entrance. In which direction is it?

train-s7q2.question: A person faces west and turns 90° to the right. Which direction do they face?

train-s7q3.question: A rectangular floor is 6 m long and 4 m wide. What is its area?

train-s7q4.question: Three sections of hose are 15 m, 20 m and 25 m long. What is their combined length?

train-s7q5.question: A corridor has doors at 5 m intervals. The first door is at 5 m. Where is the fourth door?

train-s7q6.question: A team travels 30 m north, then 10 m south. Where is it relative to the start?

train-s7q7.question: On a diagram, a valve is between a tank and a pump. What is the order from the tank?

train-s8q1.question: A service departs at 08:35 and arrives at 09:20. What is the journey time?

train-s8q2.question: A service is due at 16:48 and is 12 minutes late. What is the revised arrival time?

train-s8q3.question: A route is 90 km long. At an average speed of 60 km/h, what is the travel time?

train-s8q4.question: A schedule allows 4 minutes at each of 3 stops. What is the total stopping time?

train-s8q5.question: A vehicle travels 24 km in 20 minutes. What is its average speed?

train-s8q6.question: A working period starts at 11:15 and ends at 13:45. How long is it?

train-s8q7.question: Five carriages each have 64 seats. How many seats are there in total?

train-s9q1.question: A supply box holds 24 items. Six are used. What fraction remains?

train-s9q2.question: A task begins at 14:35 and lasts 50 minutes. When does it finish?

train-s9q3.question: Four equal groups share 36 items. How many items are in each group?

train-s9q4.question: A reading rises from 40 to 50. What is the percentage increase?

train-s9q5.question: A plan uses a scale of 1 cm to 2 m. What distance does 6 cm represent?

train-s9q6.question: Three loads weigh 12 kg, 15 kg and 18 kg. What is their total mass?

train-s9q7.question: A checklist has 20 items. Four remain unchecked. What percentage is complete?

train-s10q1.question: Two people give different times for the same event. What is the best next step?

answers.a1: Check each account against other reliable information
answers.a2: Choose the more confident speaker automatically
answers.a3: Average the times and call that a fact

train-s10q2.question: Which statement records an observation rather than an assumption about motive?

answers.a1: The person never cared about the meeting
answers.a2: The person intended to mislead everyone
answers.a3: The person left because they were guilty
answers.a4: The person left the room at 14:10

train-s10q3.question: A photograph has no known date or location. What should be checked before relying on it?

answers.a4: Whether it matches a preferred conclusion

train-s10q4.question: A claim is repeated by three websites, all quoting one unnamed source. What does that show?

answers.a1: Proof that no further checking is needed
answers.a3: Repeated reporting, not three independent confirmations
answers.a4: Proof that the claim is accurate

train-s10q5.question: All authorised visitors have a pass. Mira has a pass. What follows from that rule alone?

answers.a1: Mira cannot be an authorised visitor
answers.a2: Mira must be an authorised visitor
answers.a4: It does not prove Mira is an authorised visitor

train-s10q6.question: A new reliable fact contradicts your initial explanation. What is the sound response?

answers.a3: Change the fact to fit the explanation
answers.a4: Treat your first idea as unchangeable

train-s10q7.question: A report says an event happened after a change. Does that timing alone prove the change caused it?

answers.a3: Yes; if the report is long enough
answers.a4: No; earlier events can never cause later ones
